news.title: Valid certificates, stolen accounts: how attackers broke npm's last trust signal
news.summary_raw: On May 19, 633 malicious npm package versions passed Sigstore provenance verification. They were cleared by the system because the attacker had generated valid signing certificates from a compromised maintainer account.Sigstore worked exactly as designed: it verified the package was built in a CI environment, confirmed a valid certificate was issued, and recorded everything in the transparency log. What it cannot do is determine whether the person holding the credentials authorized the publish —
news.summary: Attackers compromised an npm maintainer account to generate valid signing certificates, breaching Sigstore's trust signal. This highlights a limitation of automated verification systems that only check for technical correctness, rather than malicious intent.
news.enterprise_use: Check your code signing and package management workflows to ensure you don't rely solely on automated verification. Inaction means potential security breaches from malicious packages with valid certificates. JumpCloud can help with robust IAM and access controls to minimize the impact of compromised accounts.
